Hello, I think I have the wrong company but I'm not sure, so I'll explain. I bought a subscription to a meal planning app about three weeks ago, and I'm trying to cancel it, but I can't remember the name of the company. My bank statement shows a charge of 9.99 from something that starts with "OUR", so I searched online and found your website. Is this you? The app I remember had recipes and a shopping list feature and a green logo with a carrot on it. If it's not you, I'm sorry for bothering you. If it is you, please cancel it. My email is probably jane.whitmore64@aol.com but I have a few different emails, so it might be another one.

subject: Overcharged and can't reach anyone
body:
Hi,

I'm writing because I've been overcharged, and every attempt to contact your billing team has gone nowhere. Your chatbot sends me in circles, and the billing email address only returns an automated message saying someone will reply within 48 hours. That was six days ago.

Here's the problem: in September we reduced our seats from 20 to 12, and I received a confirmation email. Our October invoice (INV-64221) still charged for 20 seats, $280 instead of $168. Our November invoice (INV-64998) did the same. That's $224 we've been overcharged.

I'd like a refund of $224, confirmation that our seat count is actually 12 in your billing system, and for someone to reply to me within the next two days. I don't want to raise a dispute with our card provider, but I will if I have to.

Account: acct_ox4412

Regards,
Stephen Clarke
Finance Director, Oxley Architecture

We're a small family business (four of us) and we've been paying for the Business plan for the last 8 months, because when we signed up, the person on the sales chat told us we needed Business to share projects with our customers. Last week I found out from a friend that the free guest feature on the Pro plan does exactly what we need. I checked, and it's true. So we've been paying about $60 a month more than necessary for 8 months, because of what your sales person told us. I'd like to be moved to Pro and refunded the difference for those months. I saved the chat transcript, if that helps. Workspace: bakers-dozen-catering.ourapp.com. I'm not trying to be difficult, I just think it's fair, since we followed your advice.

subject: Email notifications stopped after SSO rollout
body:
Hello,

We rolled out Azure AD SSO for our workspace last Tuesday, and it went smoothly: everyone can log in. But since the rollout, nobody receives any email notifications from your app. No assignments, mentions or digests. In-app and push notifications still work.

We wondered whether the SSO change affected users' email addresses. Our Azure AD sends the UPN (which is firstname.lastname@corp.harbourline.com) rather than the primary email (firstname.lastname@harbourline.com). If your system updated everyone's email to the UPN on first SSO login, the notifications might be going to addresses that don't receive mail.

Could you check whether that's what happened? And if so, what's the fix: changing the SAML attribute on our side, correcting the addresses in bulk on yours, or both? We have 140 users affected.

Org ID: 73305

Thanks,
James Whitfield
IT Systems Manager

Our payment failed this month and I'm trying to sort it out, but I've found a bigger problem along the way. The card on file belongs to our previous finance manager, who left the company in the summer. When she left, she cancelled her company card, which is why the payment failed. But she's also still listed as the billing contact and the account owner, so all the billing emails go to her old address, and none of us can change the payment method, because only the owner can. I'm the new finance manager and I'm an admin in the workspace. How do we update the card, change the billing contact to me, and transfer ownership, all before the account gets suspended? The warning says 5 days. Workspace: tallis-accounting.ourapp.com, my email: f.osei@tallisaccounting.com.

subject: Security questionnaire for tender
body:
Dear Sales and Security teams,

We're a public sector organisation in the Netherlands, and we're running a formal tender for a project management platform. Your company has been invited to submit a proposal.

As part of the tender, all bidders must complete the attached security and privacy questionnaire (which I'll send once you confirm a contact) and provide:
- ISO 27001 certification, with the scope statement
- A current penetration test summary from an independent third party
- Confirmation that all data is stored and processed within the EU
- A signed Data Processing Agreement based on our template, compliant with the Dutch Government Information Security Baseline (BIO)

The deadline for submissions is five weeks from today. Please confirm your intention to bid and nominate a contact person for questions.

With kind regards,
Ingrid de Vries
Procurement Officer, Gemeente Westerland

I've been trying to use your app for the past month to manage my freelance writing work, and I have to be honest: I'm struggling. I'm sure it's partly me, because I'm not very technical, but everything feels more complicated than it needs to be. When I want to add a simple to-do, I have to pick a project, a section, a status and a priority, and the form won't let me skip them. When I finish something, I can't find where it went. I just want a simple list of what I need to do today and this week, sorted by deadline. My friend uses your app and loves it, so I think I'm missing something. Could someone explain the simplest way to set it up for just one person with a list of articles and deadlines? My email is imogen.farrow.writes@gmail.com.
